findings.title: Mutable default evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the dataclass is defined (at module import), not per-instance. All AssignmentSource instances that don't explicitly pass `queued` will share the same timestamp (the time the module was imported), not the actual time the assignment occurred. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: where_should_sync does not pass sync_source to should_sync
findings.body: `where_should_sync` calls `integration.get_installation(...).should_sync(key)` without passing an `AssignmentSource`, so this path never applies cycle-breaking logic. This is only used for inbound sync currently, but if later reused with sync_source context it would silently ignore the loop-prevention check.

findings.title: remove_old_assignees runs even when outbound sync is skipped due to source
findings.body: The `assign`/`deassign` logic still records activity, history, and calls remove_old_assignees regardless of whether sync_group_assignee_outbound actually propagates (it's guarded only by the feature flag, not by whether should_sync will reject due to matching assignment_source). This isn't itself wrong, but the outbound skip logic is only enforced deep in task/installation code, meaning multiple analytics/activity records could still be generated per cycle even though the external sync is suppressed - worth confirming this is intended for the cycle-breaking goal of this PR, since activity/history records could still loop-generate even if the direct Jira sync does not.
